title: Don't Switch Your Medicare Plan Until You Watch This (2027)

shots.spoken: If you plan to shop your Medicare coverage this fall, watch this first before making a very costly mistake.
Every fall, I talk to folks who switched plans to save forty dollars a month, and it cost them thousands.
Worse yet, many realized too late that they could never get their original Medicare coverage back.
I am Arric. I have been in the insurance business since 1994, helping people navigate Medicare with confidence.
Twenty twenty-seven is a massive year for Medicare changes. Supplement rates are climbing, and millions face plan cancellations.
Plus, many standalone drug plans will cost much more next year because temporary federal subsidies are ending December thirty-first.
Today, I will walk you through how to safely shop your Medicare Supplement, Medicare Advantage, and Part D plans.
Stick around until the end, where I share our Rate Increase Hack to lower your supplement costs without sacrificing protection.
Let us start with the coverage where one wrong move is hardest to undo: your Medicare Supplement, or Medigap plan.
The biggest misconception is thinking the fall Annual Enrollment Period lets you freely switch Medigap plans without health questions.
From October fifteenth to December seventh, anyone can change their Medicare Advantage or Part D prescription drug plan.
However, that fall window gives you zero special rights to change your Medicare Supplement policy without medical underwriting.
Everyone gets one six-month Medigap Open Enrollment window when they first turn sixty-five and enroll in Medicare Part B.
Once that six-month window closes, switching Medigap plans or carriers in most states requires passing health underwriting questions.
That means an insurance company can legally review your health history, charge you higher rates, or decline your application completely.
Now, several states do offer special Birthday Rules or Anniversary Rules that let existing policyholders switch without health questions.
However, state rules vary wildly. In states like Kentucky or West Virginia, you can only switch within your current carrier.
Irony is, states with Birthday Rules are seeing the steepest rate hikes because carriers must accept higher-risk applicants guaranteed issue.
Years ago, Medigap rate increases averaged five to eight percent, and premiums over two hundred fifty dollars were rare.
Today, standard Plan G rates are climbing rapidly, pushing many beneficiaries to consider Plan N or High-Deductible Plan G.
Plan N is a strong alternative to Plan G. You still only pay the standard annual Medicare Part B deductible.
The tradeoff with Plan N is paying up to twenty dollars for doctor visits and fifty dollars for emergency rooms.
Plan N also does not cover Part B excess charges, though very few doctors nationwide actually bill for those today.
Meanwhile, High-Deductible Plan G is surging in popularity. For twenty twenty-seven, the annual deductible is three thousand fifty dollars.
You do not pay full medical prices toward that deductible; you only pay the twenty percent Medicare coinsurance share.
Think of that three thousand fifty dollars as an annual out-of-pocket maximum before the plan pays one hundred percent.
If you have chronic conditions or see specialists frequently, staying on traditional Plan G may still be your best value.
Remember, if you downgrade from Plan G, getting your old Plan G back later will likely require passing medical underwriting.
When shopping Medigap, remember that policies do not reset January first; rates typically adjust on your policy anniversary month.
Also, Medigap benefits are standardized by law. A Plan G or Plan N offers identical medical coverage across every carrier.
However, underwriting questions vary by company. One carrier might decline a health condition while another carrier approves you immediately.
Golden rule: never cancel your current Medigap policy until your new policy is officially approved and in your hands.
Also, getting approved for a new Medigap policy does not automatically cancel your old one. You must call to cancel.
We have seen folks accidentally pay for two Medigap plans for months because they assumed the switch happened automatically.
Finally, you can shop Medigap three hundred sixty-five days a year. Waiting until after December seventh often means faster processing.
Next, let us cover Medicare Advantage. Over three million beneficiaries are on Advantage plans that are terminating for twenty twenty-seven.
Major carriers like Humana, UnitedHealthcare, and Aetna are exiting unprofitable counties and shrinking provider networks across the country.
Check your mail for your Annual Notice of Change, or log into Medicare dot gov to verify your plan status.
Scenario one: your Advantage plan is completely non-renewed. If you do nothing, you are dropped back to Original Medicare alone.
However, a plan termination gives you a special Guaranteed Issue right to buy certain Medigap plans without any health questions.
Scenario two: your carrier crosswalks you into a different Advantage plan automatically. Check the new doctor network and drug formulary.
Scenario three: your Advantage plan renews, but copays, maximum out-of-pocket limits, or extra dental benefits may still change quietly.
Do not rely solely on Medicare dot gov for Advantage shopping, as fine-print benefit details are often incomplete online.
If you want to leave Medicare Advantage for Medigap, you must pass medical underwriting unless you have a special right.
Special rights include a plan termination, living in a continuous enrollment state, or using your twelve-month first-time Trial Right.
Always get your Medigap approval first, then enroll in a standalone Part D plan, which automatically cancels your Advantage plan.
And remember the Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period from January first to March thirty-first allows one additional plan switch.
For standalone Part D drug plans, premiums are rising across the board, though budget options like Wellcare Value Script remain.
Never pick a drug plan just for a low premium. Always calculate your total annual cost based on your exact prescriptions.
Now for the Rate Increase Hack: pairing a low-premium High-Deductible Plan G with targeted hospital indemnity and cancer policies.
If you are hospitalized or diagnosed with cancer, these ancillary plans pay direct cash benefits straight to you.
You use that cash to wipe out your three thousand fifty dollar deductible, while enjoying much lower monthly premiums overall.
Even better, High-Deductible Plan G rates historically increase much slower than standard Plan G, saving you thousands long term.
Do not guess your way through enrollment. Comment GUIDE below for our interactive checklist, or visit allen and associates dot agency.
